purpose: Conceptual classroom sketches; not experimental coordinate data

generation_prompts.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create one clean hand-drawn line-art teaching illustration for a beginner biology cookbook, suitable for an elementary-school learner. Square composition with TWO large panels stacked vertically. Plain white paper background, charcoal pencil outlines with slight natural wobble, simple flat pale colors, generous space. NO written text, NO letters, NO numbers, NO logos, NO watermark: bilingual labels will be supplied separately outside the image. Top panel: a friendly abstract green protein shape drawn like a folded bead-chain forming a clear small concave groove, and a small orange connected-stick-shaped drug next to the groove. A single simple blue arrow points from the orange piece toward that groove. Bottom panel: exactly the same green protein shape and orange drug shape, now with the orange drug inside that groove; highlight just a few nearby green beads using thin purple circles, and ONE dashed blue straight ruler-like line between a drug atom and a nearby protein bead. This is a conceptual analogy, not a true molecular structure. Do not draw a complete key, padlock, pill, tablet, person, drug packaging, chemical formula, hydrogen bond notation, atom labels, energy chart, tumor, before/after health claim or claim of efficacy. Avoid an image suggesting every neighboring bead forms a chemical bond. Keep the drug obviously much smaller than the protein; no extra orange fragments. Large, readable shapes and restrained green/orange/blue/purple colors matching the real lesson figures. Polished simple classroom sketch, not a photorealistic molecule, not a dense infographic.

Use case: scientific-educational. Create one clean hand-drawn line-art teaching illustration for a beginner biology cookbook, suitable for an elementary-school learner. Square composition with TWO large panels stacked vertically. Plain white paper background, charcoal pencil outlines with slight natural wobble, simple flat pale colors, generous space. NO written text, NO letters, NO numbers, NO logos, NO watermark: bilingual labels will be supplied separately outside the image. Top panel: a large abstract green protein surface shaped like a smooth bean with a small shallow curved surface patch, and an antibody Fab FRAGMENT beside it. Draw the Fab fragment as ONLY TWO short adjacent folded bead-strings, orange for its light chain and blue for its heavy chain, together forming one small hand-like curved contact tip. Do NOT draw a full Y-shaped antibody, Fc stem, two arms or a human hand. A single blue arrow indicates approaching the green surface. Bottom panel: exactly the same green surface and same two-color Fab fragment meeting at ONE LOCAL SURFACE PATCH; both orange and blue tips approach that patch. Circle a few nearby beads in purple on both sides and use only TWO dashed proximity lines across the interface. Dashed lines are geometric proximity, not chemical bonds. The Fab stays outside and touches the surface, not inside a deep pocket, and does not surround the whole green protein. This is a conceptual analogy, not a true molecular structure or a validated epitope. Do not include a membrane, whole cell, sugar, drug packaging, pills, chemical formulas, hydrogen bond labels, energy charts, tumor or a cure claim. Large, readable shapes with green target, orange light chain and blue heavy chain consistent across both panels. Polished simple classroom sketch, not a photorealistic molecule, not a dense infographic.

revision_prompts.prompt: Edit this teaching sketch with exactly one correction: the orange drug must have the SAME FIVE orange atom circles and the SAME connectivity in both panels. The top panel already has five atoms; the bottom currently has only four. In the bottom panel add the missing leftmost terminal orange circle, connected by a short stick to the existing left orange circle, so it exactly matches the top drug graph (two-circle left chain into the central circle, with the two right branches). Keep the top panel entirely unchanged. Preserve the protein shape, white paper, charcoal pencil style, two-panel layout, colors, arrow, purple neighbor circles and blue dashed distance mark. Do not add text, labels, new atoms elsewhere, chemical bonds to the protein, or a full key/padlock. The drug does not gain or lose atoms when moved into a pocket.

Edit this teaching sketch to correct the bottom panel INTERFACE DISTANCE MARKS. The current purple dashed marks wrongly connect the orange and blue Fab chains to each other. Remove those two dashed marks and the solid purple overlay circles covering the Fab beads. Add TWO small GREEN target-residue circles embedded visibly along the boundary of the large green protein at the contact patch, outlined in charcoal and circled with thin purple rings. Add exactly TWO dashed blue or purple distance lines ACROSS the antibody–target interface: one from an orange Fab-tip bead to one green target circle, the other from a blue Fab-tip bead to the other green target circle. Every dashed-line pair must have ONE Fab endpoint and ONE GREEN target-protein endpoint; never connect the two Fab chains to each other with a dashed line. Preserve the white paper, charcoal pencil style, two stacked panels, green target shape, orange light-chain and blue heavy-chain colors, no full Y antibody, the top arrow, and the overall surface-recognition scene. Do not add text, labels, clinical effect symbols or a deep pocket. These dashed marks depict geometric proximity only.
